draft_notes.explanation: Synthetic visibility contract: every latent row band and column band retains at least one nonbackground input pixel. Random generator resamples only when an entire band is erased. Existing explicit fixtures are unchanged. Under this contract the source enumerates every compatible2..4band layout,including fully erased individual blocks. Unknown blocks or rival grids cause rejection; no greedy/majority fallback. All retained mosaic grids agree. Mirror axis is learned from demonstrations and query predictions must agree; factory ignores d4.
draft_notes.explicit_domain_change: The former unrestricted punching domain admits the canonical test input with both3-column and4-column labels. Its alternative fourth band is completely erased, so input cannot reveal that label. This is a real identical-input/different-output witness, not merely poor performance. The new documented observable-band contract removes only these unobservable latent dimensions. No grid dimensions, band counts, widths, colours, partial erasure patterns, or same-colour neighbours are otherwise restricted. Individual erased blocks remain possible and are rejected by visible identifiability gating when they create unresolved colour choices.

draft_notes.full_erased_block_handling: Unknown blocks are included in enumeration. Every unknown cell has at most4adjacent cells and9possible nonbackground colours; assigning different colours from neighbours satisfies all adjacent-band nonidentity conditions and leaves multiple choices. Thus any such compatible layout proves ambiguity. A native-valid all-bands-visible twin witness is saved for seed80200069.
draft_notes.independent_gate: arc_agi2.mosaic_band_evidence uses exhaustive Cartesian products of band lengths and independent block-set checks. Source uses recursive cuts pruned by monochrome interval extents. Both deduplicate only equivalent visible-line assignments and include unknown cells. Gate needs demonstration outputs and query inputs only.
